analysis:
Examined the head text of StandaloneServer.swift (lines 1782-2288, ensureModelLoaded) and the LaunchAgent.swift patch plus base text. The StandaloneServer change visible here is the added releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad (from the patch) and its use in ensureMemoryHeadroomForLoad. The load path is shown only as context. It releases retained free KV segments and clears the MLX buffer pool once before evicting an LRU idle slot. That is a memory-availability and DoS posture change. It adds no new data flow, network surface or authorization decision. Relevant threats: T-028 (residual GPU memory) and T-041 (cache and KV). Nothing visible weakens the encrypted SSD tier, the HMAC lookup names, the TTL or the account-scoped cacheSalt.

The LaunchAgent change adds three env keys to the launchd passthrough allowlist: idle cache sweep, segment retention and segment host zeros. They are forwarded only when non-empty and only by exact key name. The allowlist stays fixed, so no arbitrary environment injection is possible. The values are operator-controlled rollback switches in the operator's own plist, and the operator is already ADV-001 with local control. The keys correctly reach the watchdog-restarted job. I saw no change to the plist file permissions, to the worker opt-in handling or to the App Attest keys.

Unverified contract: the implementations of GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments, busyEnginesKeepReclaimableMemory, retained or host-zeroed segment retention and the idle cache sweep are outside the supplied evidence. T-028 (residual KV data in GPU memory) depends on whether retained segments are zeroed before reuse across tenants. The DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS key suggests zeroing exists, but this cannot be confirmed from this batch. Further review should check that retention and reuse in the engine and KV budget files do not leak cross-request KV contents, and that the env parsing defaults are fail-safe. No finding is raised because no concrete regression is visible.
